header.title: OTAs may stay resilient to agentic AI via inventory breadth and consumer browsing habits

s01_bottom_line.text: Morgan Stanley argues agentic AI's impact on OTAs may be balanced, with their broad inventory making them valuable to AI agents and consumers continuing to browse before booking.
The article suggests OTAs may remain resilient and could even gain if AI becomes a discovery source reducing paid-search spend.
OTAs face a disruption risk from direct-booking agents but could retain relevance; the net effect on OTA revenue is unquantified and uncertain.

items.text: OTAs' broad hotel inventory breadth could make them valuable to AI agents seeking the best match.
Agentic AI's impact on OTAs may be balanced, with potential advantages as well as risks.
How much booking activity actually shifts between hotel and OTA channels remains uncertain.
AI agents as a new discovery source could help OTAs generate bookings while spending less on traditional paid search, and OTA loyalty programs could influence which links an agent recommends.
Consumers often search and compare options multiple times before booking, and agentic AI may not change that habit entirely, supporting continued OTA relevance.
